subject.title: fix(doctor): preserve allowlist entries for version-bound runtime plugins during stale config scan

question: Should `doctor --fix` preserve allow-only `codex` entries permanently, or only while the version-bound externalization install or migration is pending or failed?
rationale: The patch changes upgrade cleanup semantics for persisted user configuration, and source/tests cannot establish whether a permanently stale Codex entry should remain protected after the externalization window.

options.title: Bound preservation to migration
options.body: Preserve `codex` only while the version-matched install or backfill is pending or failed, then let ordinary stale cleanup resume.

options.title: Preserve permanently
options.body: Treat every version-bound runtime plugin ID as non-removable by doctor sequencing and document this compatibility contract.

options.title: Pause this patch
options.body: Hold the PR until the broader missing-harness readiness and externalization migration behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Bound preservation to migration
recommendation.body: Preserve `codex` only while the version-matched install or backfill is pending or failed, then let ordinary stale cleanup resume.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans the configured runtime collector and missing configured plugin repair boundary where this policy is best owned.
